chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Bukayr ibn A'yan, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them).

Regarding a man who caught an antelope in the unrestricted area (al-Hill), so he bought it and brought it into the Sanctuary (al-Haram), and the antelope died in the Sanctuary. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If when he brought it into the Sanctuary he freed its way (so it could leave) and it died, then there is nothing upon him; and if he kept it until it died with him in the Sanctuary, then upon him is the expiation (fidyah).'

key_terms.الْحِلّ: The unrestricted area outside the sacred boundaries of Mecca
key_terms.الْفِدَاءُ: Expiation or compensation for a religious violation
key_terms.خَلَّى سَبِيلَهُ: He freed its way (allowed it to leave)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for keeping a hunted animal inside the Haram?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the liability for hunting game within the sacred precincts of Mecca by distinguishing between accidental death and deliberate retention. The ruling hinges on whether the animal was released to leave the Haram or was kept there, establishing a precedent for intent-based jurisprudence in Shia fiqh. This distinction underscores the sanctity of the boundary and the specific obligations tied to violating it.
